subject: Dedicated capacity: scaling anchors & operational action lane
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Erin Black <erin.black@novafusion.ai>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@novafusion.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity: scaling anchors & operational action lane

Thanks again for the time this morning — great conversation. Below is a concise recap (action-oriented) so we have a clear alignment on risks, goals, and next steps. Please flag anything I missed.

Summary of customer pain and goals:
- Pain: 99th-percentile latency spikes during burst windows and occasional token-serving errors when concurrent batch inference ramps.
- Security: All traffic and logs must be isolated for PHI handling (HIPAA + SOC2 controls); procurement will require a BAA and evidence artifacts.
- Cost target: wanting to bring inference unit cost materially below current hosted provider (~target $0.002/token for steady-state), plus predictable commit pricing for budgeting.
- Goal: Reserve dedicated capacity to guarantee p99 latency SLOs while retaining controlled burst capacity for training/experimentation windows. Production target: pilot in a non-PHI environment in ~8 weeks; PHI-prod targeted Q3.

Qualitative ops constraints we noted:
- Must support model pinning/version rollouts and quick rollback policy for model regressions.
- Need audit-level access to per-route logs and token-level cost breakdown for internal chargeback.
- Preference for a private VPC-deployed control plane (for procurement/compliance reasons).

Redwood-recommended initial sizing (high level):
- Baseline reservation: 16 x A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved) for steady throughput.
- Burst pool: ability to scale to 64 GPUs for scheduled/unscheduled spikes (burst billing or short-term commit).
- Target p99 latency: <= 300ms for 32-token generations; throughput target: sustained 1k rps across key routes.
- SLA anchor: propose 99.9% uptime with credits and an ops-runbook for on-call escalation.

Attachments Im sharing now: nova_infra_requirements.xlsx (you provided), and Ill attach a Redwood ops playbook & a preliminary SLA draft in the follow-up.

Immediate next steps (owners & dates):
1) Jonas: provide an ops-playbook + SLA draft by 2026-05-13 (attached in next message).
2) Erin / Tom: confirm PHI timeline and whether the pilot can run non-PHI earlier (reply by 2026-05-14).
3) Stephanie: coordinate commercial anchors & procurement loop (intro to procurement) — propose procurement call week of 2026-05-18.
4) Marissa: scope onboarding tech deep-dive to capture model/profile specifics (schedule once procurement confirms).

Let me know if you want this converted into a mutual action plan doc (HubSpot link) — happy to generate one we can both track.

Best,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Erin Black <erin.black@novafusion.ai>

Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 12:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: scaling anchors & operational action lane

Thanks Jonas — this is helpful and captures the main points. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- HIPAA/SOC2: we will need a BAA in place before PHI ingestion. Our security team will request SOC2 Type II artifacts and an architectural diagram showing where logs live.
- Pilot window: we can do a non-PHI pilot immediately after contracts (~6 weeks), PHI-prod is blocked until the BAA + architecture review complete (target Q3 as discussed).
- Sizing: 16 baseline GPUs aligns with our preliminary throughput estimates; well validate with the test harness and come back with exact qps/token distribution.

Procurement note: Ive CCd procurement@novafusion.ai (internal distribution) to pull legal and finance into the thread. They will ask for a commercial sheet and the SLA language.

Quick ask: can Redwood provide a sample SLO & incident credit table that maps to the 99.9% anchor you mentioned? That will speed eval on our side.

Appreciate it,
Erin
Erin Black
VP Product | NovaFusion

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: scaling anchors & operational action lane

Erin — thanks for the prompt reply. Attached: redwood-dedicated-ops-playbook-v1.pdf and SLA-draft-DF-7421.pdf. Both are intentionally pragmatic so procurement/security can iterate.

Whats in the attachments (high level):
- Ops playbook: onboarding steps, model pinning, rollback cadence, KV/prefix caching controls, runbook for burst and degraded-fallback behavior.
- SLA draft: uptime tiers, remediation credits, SLO table (p50/p95/p99 latency examples), maintenance window policy, and escalation contacts.

Commercial & technical proposal (proposal-level anchors):
- Baseline: 16 reserved GPUs, monthly commit.
- Burst: configured burst pool allowing up to 64 GPUs for scheduled windows; burst charged at lower per-GPU short-term rate to avoid extreme overage spikes.
- Isolation: single-tenant VPC pool (network isolation + customer-managed KMS).
- Observability: per-route token breakdowns, trace-level sampling, and audit logs shipped to your GCS/S3 bucket.

Owners & immediate asks: 
- Stephanie Nguyen: will follow with a commercial anchor and sample SLO credit table (timeline: next business day).
- Marissa Cole: will run the onboarding checklist and book a 90-minute technical deep-dive once procurement confirms windows.
- Erin/Tom: please confirm if procurement needs any extra artifacts for the BAA/security review (reply by 2026-05-14).

If this looks aligned we can convert the attachments into a short SOW and target a procurement kickoff call the week of 2026-05-18.

Best,
Jonas

Date: Fri, 14 May 2026 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Commercial anchors for DF-7421 (baseline + burst)

Hi Erin / procurement team — looping in the commercial anchors to give you something tangible to share with finance. These are anchors (not final):

- Baseline commit: 16 GPUs (A100-eq) — list price anchor $120,000 / month (12-month committed term).
- Burst policy: up to 64 GPUs available; burst charged at usage rate for short-term capacity (we can show example monthly burn scenarios).
- Ramp credit: 2 months of 50% credit on the baseline for the first 60 days of onboarding (to offset integration/testing).
- SLA: standard 99.9% uptime with 5% service credit per 0.1% below the anchor (capped at one months fees) — see attached SLA draft.

Next step: can procurement confirm a 30–45 minute window for a procurement + legal sync on Thu, 2026-05-16? If so Ill send a calendar invite and a one-page commercial summary.

Thanks,
Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
